correctness.rationale: The source gives arbitrarily accurate projectional factorizations with product constant tending to one. Projecting to a chosen canonical block makes the target a scalar multiple of the identity; a Neumann correction produces an exact identity factorization whose product tends to the block-projection norm divided by the coefficient modulus. Two-sided composition preserves strict singularity, and a strictly singular operator cannot lie within norm less than one of the identity on an infinite-dimensional space. Taking infima yields the stated inequalities; applying the same argument to I-D uses \(\lambda_{\mathcal U}^k(I)=1\).
